progress.title: Progress
progress.empty: Nothing trained yet. Complete a training session to start seeing real progress here.
progress.noNearTransferBody: A short periodic assessment using a task you haven’t practiced directly, sharing the same underlying mechanism as one of your trained tasks, will appear here once you’ve taken one.
progress.nearTransferPremium: Near-transfer assessments are a premium feature.
progress.measuredPeriodically: Measured periodically, not every session, to avoid pure practice effects.
progress.broaderBody: Broader transfer — to general intelligence, memory in daily life, or unrelated tasks — isn’t established in current research for these exercises. We won’t show a number here until there’s real evidence behind it.

digitSpan.name: Backward Digit Span
digitSpan.enterReverse: Enter the numbers, in reverse order
digitSpan.intro: A short, different-shaped task from your trained exercises: you’ll see a sequence of digits, then enter them back in reverse order. The sequence gets longer as you succeed and stops after two misses in a row.
digitSpan.disclaimer: This measures a near-transfer working-memory outcome sharing structure with your trained tasks — it does not measure IQ, general intelligence, or everyday memory.
digitSpan.resultNote: Across the whole run you recalled {correct} of {total} sequences correctly. This is a near-transfer measure — a genuinely different task from your trained exercises that shares their working-memory span structure. It doesn’t measure IQ, general intelligence, or everyday memory, and results at a single length from a handful of trials carry real uncertainty.

spatialSpan.name: Backward Spatial Span
spatialSpan.tapReverse: Tap the squares back in reverse order
spatialSpan.intro: A short, different-shaped task from your trained exercises: squares will light up on the grid in a sequence, then you’ll tap them back in reverse order. The sequence gets longer as you succeed and stops after two misses in a row.
spatialSpan.disclaimer: This measures a near-transfer spatial working-memory outcome sharing structure with your trained Spatial Sequence exercise — it does not measure IQ, general intelligence, or everyday memory.
spatialSpan.resultNote: Across the whole run you recalled {correct} of {total} sequences correctly. This is a near-transfer measure — a genuinely different task from your trained Spatial Sequence exercise (backward instead of forward recall) that shares its working-memory span structure. It doesn’t measure IQ, general intelligence, or everyday memory, and results at a single length from a handful of trials carry real uncertainty.
